title: Fed emergency rate cut before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) holds an emergency meeting after which the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lowered between November 11, 2025 and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An emergency meeting is defined as any unscheduled meeting called by the Federal Reserve Board or the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) apart from the regular eight pre-scheduled meetings for 2025 and the regular eight pre-scheduled meetings for 2026.

The resolution source will be official announcements from the Federal Reserve’s website (federalreserve.gov) or credible news sources reporting on the emergency meeting.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent above-target inflation and a resilient U.S. economy have anchored trader expectations against any Federal Reserve emergency rate cut before 2027.** With the federal funds target range steady at 3.50–3.75% since late 2025, July 2026 PCE inflation registered 3.7% year-over-year (core 3.3%), well above the 2% goal amid supply shocks from Middle East tensions. The labor market remains stable near 4.1–4.3% unemployment, supported by solid GDP growth and productivity gains, while FOMC projections and recent minutes signal a preference for holding rates or potential modest hikes rather than easing. Market-implied odds reflect this hawkish tilt, with traders assigning only a slim chance to an unscheduled cut absent a severe crisis. A sharp escalation in geopolitical risks or sudden financial-market stress could still alter the path, though current data show no such catalysts.
